Entry Horse Herds of the Dothraki The Dothraki's wealth, identity, and freedom of movement are tied to their horses. Kaa judges the strength of horses by the number of horses, and ordinary riders judge the future of their families by the health of their mounts. People who settle in the city often misunderstand this relationship as barbarism, but in fact it is a complete life. Any break in the place of origin, checkpoints, shipping schedules, debts and protection fees will immediately make the nobles in the distance feel the changes in price and power.

Entry Horse Herds of the Dothraki The Dothraki's wealth, identity, and freedom of movement are tied to their horses. Kaa judges the strength of horses by the number of horses, and ordinary riders judge the future of their families by the health of their mounts. People who settle in the city often misunderstand this relationship as barbarism, but in fact it is a complete life. They may not necessarily understand ledgers, but they know the true weight of a bag of salt and a nail on the road.

Kaa judges the strength of horses by the number of horses, and ordinary riders judge the future of their families by the health of their mounts. People who settle in the city often misunderstand this relationship as barbarism, but in fact it is a complete life. Some people turn raw materials into tools, cloth and medicine, others set festivals and taboos for exchange; wealth is piled up by many hands, and rarely belongs to just one name.

People who settle in the city often misunderstand this relationship as barbarism, but in fact it is a complete life. If prices rise but wages do not, prosperity in distant places will only become thinner bread; if roads are safe, even small villages can get a little spring from trade.
